title: Sephiria Destiny Inscription: Upgrade Paths and Talents
description: Use the Destiny Inscription tree to unlock village systems, weapons, and talents, and check prerequisites before spending sapphires.
meta: Updated 26 October 2026. Progression reference based on the Steam Basic Guide; confirm node names and requirements in your current game.
body:
Destiny Inscription is Sephiria’s permanent meta tree. Sapphires come from dungeon depth and bosses defeated; spending them unlocks weapons, events, inventory, dice, and talent access. Use the board’s links to inspect prerequisites and choose upgrades based on the next system or weapon you want to unlock.

Two habits keep the spend cheap. Read the node’s own description before buying, and check which town feature or training step the node feeds. The tree behaves like a dependency chain rather than a list, so most wasted sapphires go to a node that looked like progress but gated nothing you could reach yet.

How the tree is organized

  • New Events / fruit skewers lines — unlock systems you will use every run.
  • Home Repairs — progresses village quests and opens Talents (talk to the relevant NPCs after unlocking).
  • Weapon training nodes — required before Morrow’s training grounds grant new weapons.
  • Hard Mode access — after Chapter II, talk to the village tree and pick the Hard Mode dialogue (current path). Older “free Destiny node” text is outdated; see the Hard Mode unlock page.

Read the tree as a sequence, not a flat list

Every branch on the board ends in a town interaction. The node is only half the unlock, and the second half decides whether the sapphires buy anything this session.

New Events. These nodes open village systems you use between runs: the Wishing Fountain that carries pre-run Artifact picks, the costume salon, and extra weapons. Because the payoff is a building rather than a stat, the confirmation is simple — walk the village after the purchase and see whether the system is usable.

Home Repairs. This line advances village quests and opens the Talents tab. Owning the unlock is not the same as owning the talents: talk to the relevant NPCs afterwards, because the tree does not hand over talent points on its own.

Weapon training. A training node is a prerequisite, not a delivery. The weapon arrives when you go to the training ground east of the village, speak to Moro (written Morrow in some guides), finish the short training sequence, and find the branch on the village rack. Community data records Greatsword, Dagger, Crossbow, Blade and Staff on that route with Sword and Shield excluded, so confirm your branch at the training ground before spending on the node. The weapons page lists the same three-step order from the other direction.

Hard Mode. This is the one entry on the board that is not a purchase any more. Chapter II plus the village tree dialogue is the whole unlock, which is why no amount of sapphires substitutes for finishing the story step first. Details are on the Hard Mode page.

What each early spend gates

SpendWhat it opensHow you confirm it workedWhat it does not replace
New Events nodeA town system used every run, including the Wishing Fountain, the costume salon and extra weaponsWalk the village and check that the system is interactableChoosing a weapon family or a build direction
Home Repairs nodeVillage quest progress and the Talents tabTalk to the NPC involved after the purchaseTalent points, which are allocated separately
Weapon training nodeThe right to train that branch with MoroFinish the training ground and look for the weapon on the rackThe weapon itself, which needs that training step
Talent allocationDefence, MP regen, Willpower and dash windows for the build you are practisingRead the talent description and test it in a runA weapon you have not unlocked, or a combo family you have not committed to
Hard Mode dialogueRoot’s Retreat stages on later runsChapter II finished, then the tree conversationNothing in the tree — there is no node to buy

Spend decision guide

Your next goalInspect on the treeConfirm before spending
Open a town systemNew Events branchRead the node description and check whether it unlocks the Wishing Fountain or another town feature.
Practice a weaponWeapon training nodesCheck both the tree prerequisite and any follow-up training-ground quest.
Improve an existing buildTalent nodes after Home RepairsMatch the talent to your chosen weapon, and confirm the current respec method in the client.

The two tables answer different questions. The decision guide starts from a goal and points at a branch; the gating table starts from a purchase and states what still has to happen in the village afterwards. Use the second one when you already know the branch and want to avoid a half-finished unlock.

Early spend order

  1. New Events lines — daily-use systems first.
  2. Home Repairs until Talents open.
  3. Weapon training for the weapon you are learning.
  4. Talents matching that weapon — respec is allowed, so early picks are not permanent.

The order is not a rule the game enforces; it is the order that keeps every purchase usable in the next run. A town system pays back on every visit, Talents pay back once you have a weapon worth tuning, and weapon training pays back only after the training ground, which needs a chapter gate first.

Talents

Once unlocked, talent points let you bias defense, MP regen, Willpower (luck-like outcomes), dash windows, and more. Guides agree you can respec—use that to match the weapon you are learning (weapons).

Version boundary: the Steam Basic Guide's main Destiny tree section is based on version 0.7.31, with some 0.7.35 updates and a later author comment correcting the Hard Mode unlock. Its exact counts and node details are not a complete 1.0+ tree map; verify names, costs, and prerequisites in the current board.

Budgeting the first few hours

Sapphires accrue across runs from dungeon depth and bosses defeated, so a purchase that turns out to be premature costs time rather than the save. That is the argument for buying the cheap, high-frequency unlocks first and leaving branch-specific training until the chapter that opens the training ground is already behind you.

Do not budget against a number from a guide. The version note above explains why published counts are snapshots rather than a price list, so read the current node before committing and treat any total someone quotes as the version they played.

Common mistakes and their causes

  • Buying a node that gates nothing you can reach yet. The usual cause is reading the branch top-down and assuming the next available node is the next useful node. Check the town interaction first, then buy the node that unlocks it.
  • Spending talent points before the weapon is settled. Talents are matched to a weapon, and a point placed for a branch you barely played describes a build you are not running. Respec makes this recoverable, not free of cost in the moment.
  • Hunting Hard Mode at the bottom of the tree. The unlock moved to the village tree dialogue, and guides that send you to Destiny Inscription are repeating early-access text.
  • Buying the training node and stopping there. The weapon is behind a conversation and a short training ground, so the node looks broken if you never visit the east side of the village.
  • Counting inventory space as free power. Unlocking inventory or storage does not change how the Side Bag works: stored items stay inactive, Tablets included. The Side Bag section covers that rule.
  • Treating node names and costs as fixed. The board has changed across patches, so a screenshot from a video is a lead, not a price list.

Quick FAQ

Where do sapphires come from?

Dungeon depth and bosses defeated — they accrue across runs, so early misses are cheap to recover.

Can you respec?

Yes — guides agree you can respec; match talents to the weapon you are learning.

Is Hard Mode a Destiny node?

Not anymore — the unlock moved to the village tree dialogue in 0.7.55 (see Root’s Retreat).

Do I need to finish the tree before I can touch Talents?

You need the Home Repairs line far enough to open the tab, and then you need to talk to the relevant NPCs. A full tree is not the requirement; the village conversation is part of the unlock, and the tree alone does not hand over points.

Is a weapon training node the same as owning the weapon?

No. The node is the prerequisite the training ground checks. The branch appears on the rack after you speak to Moro and finish the short training sequence, so buy the node when you can also walk to the training ground in the same session.

Can I skip New Events and go straight to combat upgrades?

You can, and it is the common route into a stalled save. The town systems behind New Events are the ones that change every later run — pre-run Artifact picks, costumes and additional weapons — so skipping them leaves the later purchases with nothing to amplify.

What happens if the node I read about is not on my board?

Assume a version difference first. The published tree references are early-access snapshots, so a missing node is more likely a reference mismatch than a broken save. Compare the current description with the goal you actually have, and buy toward the town interaction.

Does unlocking more inventory make the Side Bag useful?

No. Storage remains storage: items in the Side Bag do not contribute their effects, including Tablets. Move what the build needs into the active inventory and check adjacency there. The Artifacts and Tablets page covers the layout.

What this page does not cover

  • Which weapon branch to learn, and which upgrade routes people actually finish — see weapons and upgrades.
  • How to assemble a build around one or two combo families — see builds, including the Companion route.
  • Fountain capacity, rarity costs and the Willpower levels that raise it — see Wishing Fountain.
  • Which costume trade-off suits a run — see costume roster and characters and NPCs for who unlocks what.
  • The stage milestones after the Hard Mode dialogue — see Root’s Retreat.
  • The order to do things in during the first sessions — see the beginner guide.
